candidate_sentence_map.S1: Heimstaden reported stronger operating profitability in 2025 despite broadly unchanged rental income.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Rental income was SEK 15,916 million, essentially flat versus SEK 15,919 million in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Indexation and tenant improvement investments supported income, while foreign-exchange effects, privatisations, and portfolio sales offset those gains.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Annualised like-for-like rental growth was 4.9%, down from 5.6%, while real economic occupancy remained stable at 98.5%.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Fourth-quarter rental income declined 3.4% to SEK 3,945 million, although quarterly occupancy improved to 98.7%.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Net operating income increased to SEK 11,475 million from SEK 11,188 million, and the NOI margin rose to 72.1% from 70.3%.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: The improvement reflected a 6.1% reduction in property expenses to SEK 4,378 million, attributed to cost-control measures, digitalisation, operating efficiencies, and the smaller portfolio following property sales.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Utilities were an exception, increasing 5.7% because municipal price increases exceeded core inflation.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Capital expenditures were SEK 4,439 million, while tenant-improvement investments generated SEK 94 million of additional rental income at an average yield on cost of 10.8%.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The group’s reported profit before tax rose to SEK 16,012 million from SEK 10,403 million, and profit for the year increased to SEK 13,056 million from SEK 7,621 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The result benefited from a SEK 9,498 million fair-value gain on investment properties, compared with SEK 8,554 million in 2024, and realised property-divestment gains of SEK 2,207 million versus SEK 1,687 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: A SEK 3,996 million foreign-exchange gain also compared with a SEK 2,038 million loss in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: These gains were partly offset by a SEK 3,707 million goodwill impairment, primarily relating to Germany and Sweden, following higher discount rates in the Akelius goodwill impairment test.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Total comprehensive income fell to SEK 4,199 million from SEK 11,082 million because currency translation differences shifted to a SEK 8,857 million loss from a SEK 3,461 million gain.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: The privatisation programme remained central to capital allocation: 2,466 units were sold for SEK 10,664 million at a 28.9% premium to book value.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Divestments reduced rental income by SEK 538 million but generated proceeds used to reduce debt.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Interest-bearing liabilities declined to SEK 175,227 million from SEK 195,816 million, reducing net LTV to 52.2% from 56.4% and improving ICR to 2.0x from 1.9x.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Financing activity remained substantial, including SEK 59,500 million raised or refinanced by Heimstaden Bostad and SEK 13,767 million of outstanding green bonds.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Fitch affirmed Heimstaden’s B- rating but revised the outlook to Negative.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: No dividend was proposed for any share class.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, and K5 are PRESENT with core elements covered in multiple sentences. K4 (country-specific property value developments) is entirely missing. K6 (material post-reporting-period events) is missing. K7 (sustainability performance) is missing. The summary captures most high-importance financial performance metrics but lacks critical country-level property value details, post-period events, and sustainability metrics, resulting in a Generally yes rating.
